part2_upper_side.calibre_note: The M=1 count carries three different values under three conventions and they must never be interchanged. 289 = E3's `tv_hat > T(n)` PROXY for the band's lower edge (NOT a bound). 292 = the old inlined radius `(sqrt(m)+2.9604)/sqrt(n)`, which omits BOTH 0.5 factors and is exactly 2x the reference. 340 = the repo reference radius `0.5*sqrt(m/n) + 0.5*2.9604/sqrt(n)`. CANONICAL = reference radius + the D029 direct criterion (`eps_lo > 0.05`) = 340/990. The 289 -> 292 -> 340 progression must always be reported as an explicit old -> new pair with the convention named, because an unexplained jump from 29% to 34% reads as a data revision rather than a convention fix.

lower_side_count_provenance: The capped count was obtained by counting `eps_lo > 0.05` directly over all 990 raw rows of q1_eps_lo_symbol_map.json in this run, not taken from any prior report.
lower_side_full_n_note: This full-n total is PARTLY MEASURED: the upper side was measured over ALL 990 pairs, but the LOWER side was recomputed at full n for only the 5 targeted pairs. Of the full-n pass count, all but `recovered_pair_count` are capped values whose full-n behaviour was NOT re-measured, so they are ASSUMED to stay above 0.05 -- and that is the same monotonicity assumption that just failed for 4 of the 5 measured pairs, one of which moved in the WRONG direction. Honest range for the gate: [333, 336]. [SUPERSEDED by the full-n run q1_lower_side_full_n.json: the lower side is now measured at full n for ALL 990 pairs with the cap removed, assumed_pair_count = 0]
gate_measurement_breakdown: 336 is the JOINT gate (eps_lo > 0.05 AND eps_hi < 0.5), defined at k = 5. 340 is the UPPER SIDE ALONE. The 4-pair difference is exactly the pairs that pass the upper side and fail the lower side (11-51, 27-29, 35-49, 39-44). Both figures are correct; they denote different conjunctions. [SUPERSEDED by the full-n run q1_lower_side_full_n.json: the lower side is now measured at full n for ALL 990 pairs with the cap removed, assumed_pair_count = 0]

recovered_pair_count_definition: The number of the 5 capped lower-side failures whose full-n eps_lo rose above 0.05. This is NOT a prefix length — the gate is defined at k = 5 (see parameters.k). [SUPERSEDED by the full-n run q1_lower_side_full_n.json: the lower side is now measured at full n for ALL 990 pairs with the cap removed, assumed_pair_count = 0]
sensitivity_statement: The gate is 336 because exactly ONE boundary pair (21-23) crosses 0.05, and its capped value sat 0.0002 from the threshold (capped eps_lo 0.049781366 vs full-n 0.058780592). Report the gate as 336 WITH this sensitivity stated, not as a stable integer. Two companion readings must travel with it: (i) pair (35,49) moved the WRONG direction as n grew (0.043732229 -> 0.042724656), which shows that 'larger n gives a tighter lower bound' is a statistical TENDENCY, not a guarantee; (ii) pair (39,44) is bit-identical across runs because its full n (4624/5741) is BELOW the 20000 cap, so it was never capped at all -- 'no change' there means 'never bound', NOT 'stable'. This is a MEASURED sensitivity, not an unresolved assumption, and it is why the gate is reported as an integer with a named boundary pair rather than as a settled constant. [RETRACTED: this framing used the CAP margin of the boundary pair (0.0002), which belongs to the capped value -- a quantity the gate does not use. The measured full-n margins are +0.008781 (nearest passing pair) and -0.007275 (nearest failing pair), with within_0.005_count = 0. See gate_convention_sensitivity for the corrected statement. The structural fact that the gate flips 335 <-> 336 on this one pair is SEPARATE and still holds.]
boundary_pair: (21,23): capped 0.04978136643060134 -> full-n 0.05878059224502068; margin from the 0.05 line at the capped value = 0.00021863356939866 [NOTE ON SCALE: the margin quoted above is measured on the CAPPED value. The gate does not use capped values; its own nearest in-gate margin is +0.008781.]
gate_is_half_measured_historical_note: This was true while the lower side had been recomputed at full n for only 5 pairs. The full-n run (q1_lower_side_full_n.json) recomputed the lower side for all 990 pairs with the 20,000-flow cap removed, so it is now false. The superseded [333, 336] range belonged to that earlier half-measured state and no longer applies.
gate_convention_sensitivity: The gate is 336 under the canonical (full-n) convention; it would be 335 under the capped convention; the entire difference is pair (21,23) crossing 0.05. All five boundary pairs lie in the upper set. The nearest in-gate margin is +0.008781 and the nearest upper-only margin is -0.007275, with within_0.005_count = 0 -- so UNDER THE CANONICAL CONVENTION no sample sits close to the line; the convention-dependence of the gate value is the separate matter described in the first clause.
